reviewPolicy.sourcePolicy: Scope to Financial Transaction Response messages requiring large amounts of print data. Use the Segment 120 field table's R markers and its four-character Segment Length description.
reviewPolicy.dataPolicy: Symbolic response-segment design only. Do not assign a wire delimiter byte or claim complete length computation without authorized raw response fixture.
reviewPolicy.baselinePolicy: References SEG120-R-002 and the Segment 120 field table; no official Test record is modified.
reviewPolicy.promotionGate: Authorized Test review must confirm response applicability, full print-data payload, four-digit length calculation, framing, and fixture identity before promotion or execution.

requirementReferences.title: Segment Length is present, exactly 4 digits (zero-padded), and equals the segment's actual encoded length including the Segment Type field and Field Separators

sourceEvidence.quote: It is only sent on Financial Transaction Response messages requiring large amounts of print data.
sourceEvidence.interpretation: The rule applies in this source-defined response context; request messages and unrelated Electronic Mail cases do not by themselves establish applicability.

sourceEvidence.quote: 1 85 Segment Type 3 R Identifies the type of data segment being formatted. Fixed value: 120 Source: Host
sourceEvidence.interpretation: The Segment 120 response begins with required Segment Type 120, host sourced.

sourceEvidence.quote: 2 84 Segment Length 4 R Identifies the data segment’s length, including Segment Type’s length and Field Separators. Source: Host
sourceEvidence.interpretation: Field 2 / Element 84 is required, four characters, and includes Segment Type length and Field Separators.

sourceEvidence.quote: Note: There is a Field Separator between Field Nos. 1 and 2 and between Field Nos. 2 and 3.
sourceEvidence.interpretation: The field-level design must preserve the specified separators; actual wire encoding is not asserted here.

aiReviewReferences.assessment: All five AI linked case labels are request/Electronic Mail contexts rather than the source-required Financial Transaction Response context; the bounded screen found no exact Segment 120 Element 84 observation for any case. They do not demonstrate this requirement.

testScenarios.intent: For an authorized Financial Transaction Response requiring large print data, include Segment 120, fixed Segment Type 120, and required four-character Segment Length with source-specified separator positions.

testCases.assertion: A reviewed-valid Financial Transaction Response includes Segment 120 field 2 / Element 84 as a four-character length indicator.
The otherwise applicable Segment 120 response omits required field 2 / Element 84.

openQuestions: Confirm a source-approved large-print Financial Transaction Response context and corresponding response body.
Confirm the four-character length calculation from the complete response payload and separators.
Confirm the converter's actual Field Separator representation and bind it to raw response bytes.
Review TC-012688 approved/candidate copies; two approved payload paths are missing from frozen inventory.
